answer: A inlet of per-task receipts records who did what, and the walnut of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, forfeited on duplicate submission, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Reaching the cedar of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short.
